QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is setting up a Category I AIF to acquire stressed loans under the IBC 2016 and to finance companies that have defaulted to banks for more than 90 days. As the Manager's compliance head, which specific Category I sub-category must the fund register under?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, Special Situations Fund is a Category I AIF sub-category for distressed debt. Permitted activities include (i) participation in debt resolutions under IBC 2016 (and acting as a resolution applicant), (ii) financing companies in default to banks/NBFCs for not less than 90 days, and (iii) acquiring stressed loans and security receipts. Ms. Shah's mandate matches all three, so SSF is the correct sub-category. The Trap: Infrastructure Funds invest in infrastructure SPVs, not distressed debt. SME Funds invest in MSMEs. Venture Capital Funds invest in early-stage unlisted companies. None of these sub-categories permit acquiring stressed loans or financing 90-day defaults. Note: The SSF's permitted-asset list in the source is narrow (IBC resolution participation, 90-day-default financing, stressed loans and security receipts). General private-credit lending sits under a Cat II Debt Fund instead.
